Main.sentence: Hyde Park is a neighborhood on the ___E:South Side U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Side,_Chicago)___ of ___E:Chicago U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicago)___ , Illinois, located on and near the shore of ___E:Lake Michigan U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lake_Michigan)___ 7 miles (11 km) south of ___E:the Loop U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicago_Loop)___ .
It is one of the city's 77 ___E:community areas U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Community_areas_of_Chicago)___ .

Hyde Park is home to the ___E:University of Chicago U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Chicago)___ and several ___E:seminaries U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seminary)___ and graduate schools of ___E:theology U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Theology)___ : ___E:Catholic Theological Union U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Catholic_Theological_Union)___ , the ___E:Lutheran School of Theology at Chicago U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lutheran_School_of_Theology_at_Chicago)___ , the ___E:Chicago Theological Seminary U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicago_Theological_Seminary)___ , and ___E:McCormick Theological Seminary U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/McCormick_Theological_Seminary)___ (in addition to, UChicago's own ___E:Divinity School U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Chicago_Divinity_School)___ ).

The ___E:Griffin Museum of Science and Industry U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Museum_of_Science_and_Industry_(Chicago))___ and two of Chicago's four historic sites listed in the original 1966 ___E:National Register of Historic Places U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Register_of_Historic_Places)___ — ___E:Chicago Pile-1 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicago_Pile-1)___ , the world's first artificial ___E:nuclear reactor U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nuclear_reactor)___ , and ___E:Robie House U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robie_House)___ —are also in the neighborhood.

In the early 21st century, Hyde Park received national attention for its association with U.S. president ___E:Barack Obama U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama)___ , who, before running for president, was a Senior Lecturer for twelve years at the ___E:University of Chicago Law School U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Chicago_Law_School)___ , an ___E:Illinois state senator U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Illinois_state_senator)___ representing the area, and U.S. senator from Illinois.

The ___E:Barack Obama Presidential Center U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama_Presidential_Center)___ is currently under construction in ___E:Jackson Park U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jackson_Park,_Chicago)___ , on its border with Hyde Park.
Hyde Park's boundaries and subdivisions have several local definitions.

The community area's formal boundaries are 51st Street (signed locally as Hyde Park Boulevard) on the north, ___E:Midway Plaisance U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Midway_Plaisance)___ on the south, ___E:Washington Park U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Washington_Park_(Chicago_park))___ on the west, and Lake Michigan on the east.  Another local definition considers a section to the north between 47th Street  and Hyde Park Boulevard to be in Hyde Park, although this area is, according to municipal boundaries, the southern half of the ___E:Kenwood U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenwood,_Chicago)___ community area. As such, it is often called "South Kenwood".

Hyde Park and South Kenwood are also sometimes collectively termed "Hyde Park-Kenwood" (as in the name of the ___E:epoynmous Historic District U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hyde_Park-Kenwood_Historic_District)___ , for example).

Meanwhile, the portion of Hyde Park that lies between the ___E:Illinois Central Railroad U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Illinois_Central_Railroad)___ tracks and the lake is usually referred to as "East Hyde Park" and is usually also taken to include " ___E:Indian Village U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_Village,_Chicago)___ ", the small southeastern corner of Kenwood.

In 1853, ___E:Paul Cornell U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paul_Cornell_(lawyer))___ , a real estate speculator and cousin of ___E:Cornell University U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cornell_University)___ founder ___E:Ezra Cornell U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ezra_Cornell)___ , purchased 300 acres (1.2 km 2 ) of land  between 51st and 55th streets along the shore of ___E:Lake Michigan U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lake_Michigan)___ ,  with the idea of attracting other Chicago businessmen and their families to the area.  The neighborhood was named after a ___E:hamlet U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hyde_Park_(CDP),_New_York)___ on the ___E:Hudson River U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hudson_River)___ of the same name in ___E:New York U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_(state))___ .
The land was located seven miles south of Downtown Chicago in a rural area that enjoyed weather tempered by the lake – cooler in the summer and warmer in the winter.
It was conveniently located near the ___E:Illinois Central Railroad U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Illinois_Central_Railroad)___ , which had been constructed two years earlier.
Cornell successfully negotiated land in exchange for a railroad station at 53rd Street.
Hyde Park quickly became a suburban retreat for affluent Chicagoans who wanted to escape the noise and congestion of the rapidly growing city.
In 1857, the ___E:Hyde Park House U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hyde_Park_House)___ , an upscale hotel, was built on the shore of Lake Michigan near the 53rd Street railroad station.

For two decades, the Hyde Park House served as a focal point of Hyde Park social life. During this period, it was visited or lived in by many prominent guests, including ___E:Mary Todd Lincoln U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mary_Todd_Lincoln)___ , who lived there with her children for two and a half months in the summer of 1865 (shortly after her husband was assassinated).

The Hyde Park House burned down in an 1879 fire. The ___E:Sisson Hotel U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sisson_Hotel)___ was built on the site in 1918 and was eventually converted into a condominium building (the ___E:Hampton House U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hampton_House_(Chicago,_Illinois))___ ).
In 1861, Hyde Park was incorporated into an independent township (called ___E:Hyde Park Township U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hyde_Park_Township,_Cook_County,_Illinois)___ ).

Its boundaries were Pershing Road (39th Street) on the north, 138th Street on the south, ___E:State Street U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/State_Street_(Chicago))___ on the west, and ___E:Lake Michigan U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lake_Michigan)___ and the ___E:Indiana U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indiana)___ state line on the east.  The territory of the township encompassed most of what is now the ___E:South Side of Chicago U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Side,_Chicago)___ .

Hyde Park Township remained independent of Chicago until it was annexed to the city in 1889.  After annexation, the definition of Hyde Park as a Chicago neighborhood was restricted to the historic core of the former township, centered on Cornell's initial development between 51st and 55th streets near the lakefront.
The Hyde Park Herald , the neighborhood's community newspaper, was established in 1882 and continues to be published weekly.

In 1891, two years after the city of Chicago annexed Hyde Park,  the ___E:University of Chicago U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Chicago)___ was established in the neighborhood through the philanthropy of ___E:John D. Rockefeller U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_D._Rockefeller)___ and the leadership of ___E:William Rainey Harper U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_Rainey_Harper)___ .

In 1893, Hyde Park hosted the ___E:World's Columbian Exposition U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World%27s_Columbian_Exposition)___ (a ___E:world's fair U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World%27s_fair)___ marking the 400th anniversary of ___E:Christopher Columbus U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Columbus)___ ' arrival in the ___E:New World U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_World)___ ).

The World's Columbian Exposition brought fame to the neighborhood, which gave rise to an inflow of new residents and spurred new development that gradually started transforming Hyde Park into a more urban area. However, since most of the structures built for the fair were temporary, it left few direct traces in the neighborhood.

The only major structure from the fair that is still standing today is ___E:Charles Atwood U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charles_B._Atwood)___ 's Palace of Fine Arts, which has since been converted into the ___E:Museum of Science and Industry U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Museum_of_Science_and_Industry_(Chicago))___ .
In the early decades of the twentieth century, many upscale hotels were built in Hyde Park (mostly along the lakefront).
Hyde Park became a resort area in Chicago.

Most of these hotels closed during the ___E:Great Depression U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Great_Depression_in_the_United_States)___ , and were eventually converted into apartment and condominium buildings (most of which are still standing today).

Historical images of Hyde Park can be found in ___E:Explore Chicago Collections U:(http://explore.chicagocollections.org/records/?f2-types=Digital+Images&f1-neighborhoods=Hyde%20Park)___ , a digital repository made available by ___E:Chicago Collections U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicago_Collections)___ archives, libraries and other cultural institutions in the city.

Until the middle of the twentieth century, Hyde Park remained an almost exclusively ___E:white U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/White_American)___ neighborhood (despite its proximity to Chicago's ___E:Black Belt U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/History_of_African_Americans_in_Chicago)___ ).

Hyde Parkers relied on ___E:racially restrictive covenants U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Covenant_(law)#Exclusionary_covenants)___ to keep ___E:African Americans U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/African_American)___ out of the neighborhood.
At the time, the use of such covenants was supported by the University of Chicago.

After the ___E:Supreme Court U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Supreme_Court_of_the_United_States)___ banned racially restrictive covenants in 1948, African Americans began moving into Hyde Park, and the neighborhood gradually became multiracial.
In 1955, civil rights activist ___E:Leon Despres U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leon_Despres)___ was elected alderman of Hyde Park and held the position for twenty years.

Despres argued passionately for ___E:racial integration U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Racial_integration)___ and ___E:fair housing U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fair_housing)___ on the floor of the ___E:Chicago City Council U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicago_City_Council)___ , and became known as the "liberal conscience of Chicago" for often casting the sole dissenting vote against the policies of Chicago's then-mayor ___E:Richard J. Daley U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_J._Daley)___ .

During the 1950s, Hyde Park experienced economic decline as a result of the ___E:white flight U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/White_flight)___ that followed the rapid inflow of African Americans into the neighborhood.

In the 1950s and 1960s, the University of Chicago, in its effort to counteract these trends, sponsored one of the largest ___E:urban renewal U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urban_renewal)___ plans in the nation.

The plan involved the demolition and redevelopment of entire blocks of supposedly decayed buildings with the goal of creating an "interracial community of high standards."  After the plan was carried out, Hyde Park's average income soared by seventy percent, but its African American population fell by forty percent, since the substandard housing primarily occupied by low-income African Americans had been purchased, torn down, and replaced, with the residents not being able to afford to remain in the newly rehabilitated areas. [citation needed] The ultimate result of the renewal plan was that Hyde Park did not experience the economic depression that occurred in the surrounding areas and became a racially integrated middle-class neighborhood. [citation needed]

The central campus of the University of Chicago—including ___E:Pritzker School of Medicine U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pritzker_School_of_Medicine)___ , the ___E:University of Chicago Hospital U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Chicago_Hospital)___ , the historic Main Quadrangles, and the ___E:Booth School of Business U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Booth_School_of_Business)___ —is bounded by ___E:Washington Park U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Washington_Park_(Chicago_park))___ on the west, 55th Street on the north, University Ave. on the east, and 61st Street on the south, placing most of the university within Hyde Park's southwestern quadrant (with the remainder, south of ___E:the Midway U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Midway_Plaisance)___ , being in ___E:Woodlawn U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Woodlawn,_Chicago)___ ).

The university also owns a number of additional properties throughout Hyde Park, with many concentrated along a narrow corridor along 59th Street between the central campus and the ___E:Metra U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metra_Electric_District)___ tracks—including, for example, the ___E:University of Chicago Laboratory Schools U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Chicago_Laboratory_Schools)___ and ___E:International House U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Housing_at_the_University_of_Chicago#International_House)___ .
Due to the university's proximity, the blocks just east of the central campus are dominated by (privately owned) student and faculty residences.

The part of Hyde Park located east of the ___E:Metra U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metra_Electric_District)___ tracks is locally called East Hyde Park. This area, the part of Hyde Park nearest to Lake Michigan, has a large number of high-rise condominiums, many of them facing the lakefront.

Some of these condominiums are remnants of older hotels, like The Mayfair or Regents Park. In this respect, East Hyde Park differs markedly from the rest of Hyde Park, where the vast majority of residences are either three-story apartment buildings or single-family homes (with only a small number of high-rise condominiums).

Although the neighborhood bounded by 47th Street on the north, 51st Street (Hyde Park Boulevard) on the south, Cottage Grove Avenue on the west, and Lake Michigan on the east is officially the southern half of the ___E:Kenwood U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenwood,_Chicago)___ community area, it is often considered part of Hyde Park due to the two areas' shared culture and history; "Hyde Park-Kenwood" is thus sometimes applied to this collective area (as in, e.g., the " ___E:Hyde Park-Kenwood Historic District U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hyde_Park-Kenwood_Historic_District)___ ").

Some differences are nonetheless apparent: unlike Hyde Park, which is dominated by three- and four-story apartment buildings and modest family homes, southern Kenwood boasts a great many luxurious mansions, built mainly at the end of the nineteenth and the beginning of the twentieth centuries for wealthy Chicagoans.

A number of prominent Chicagoans currently reside or own homes in this area, including former U.S. president ___E:Barack Obama U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama)___ and ___E:Nation of Islam U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nation_of_Islam)___ leader ___E:Louis Farrakhan U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Louis_Farrakhan)___ .

Boxer ___E:Muhammad Ali U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Muhammad_Ali)___ and former Nation of Islam leader ___E:Elijah Muhammad U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elijah_Muhammad)___ also once resided in south Kenwood.
Hyde Park is a very racially diverse neighborhood.

Per ___E:2020 U.S. census U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_United_States_census)___ data, the neighborhood's residents are 45.6% white, 26.7% Black, 14.6% Asian, and 7.2% Hispanic, while a further 5.9% identified as belonging to two or more races.

The neighborhood's northern and southern halves exhibit some demographic differences, however: south of 55th Street, the population is predominantly white and Asian-American, with a smaller percentage of African-Americans and Hispanics.
North of 55th Street, African-Americans make up approximately half of the population, and there is a more robust Hispanic presence.

Hyde Park's location in the center of the predominantly ___E:African-American U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/African-American)___ ___E:South Side U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Side,_Chicago)___ , as well as the neighborhood's large population of affluent and upper-middle class Black residents, have made it an important cultural and political hub for Chicago's Black community.

Many of Chicago's prominent African-American politicians live or have lived in Hyde Park, including former ___E:Chicago mayor U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mayor_of_Chicago)___ ___E:Harold Washington U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harold_Washington)___ , the city's first Black mayor;  former U.S.
Senator ___E:Carol Moseley Braun U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carol_Moseley_Braun)___ , the first Black female U.S. senator;  former U.S.

President ___E:Barack Obama U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama)___ ;  ___E:Toni Preckwinkle U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Toni_Preckwinkle)___ , the current ___E:President of the Cook County Board of Commissioners U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/President_of_the_Cook_County_Board_of_Commissioners)___ ;  and ___E:Kwame Raoul U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kwame_Raoul)___ , the current ___E:Attorney General U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Illinois_Attorney_General)___ of Illinois.

The following Hyde Park community area properties have been added to the ___E:National Register of Historic Places U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Register_of_Historic_Places)___ : ___E:Chicago Beach Apartments U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicago_Beach_Apartments)___ , ___E:Arthur H. Compton House U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arthur_H._Compton_House)___ , East Park Towers, ___E:Chicago Pile-1 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicago_Pile-1)___ , ___E:Flamingo-on-the-Lake Apartments U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flamingo-on-the-Lake_Apartments)___ , ___E:Mayfair Apartments U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mayfair_Apartments)___ , ___E:Isadore H. Heller House U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Isadore_H._Heller_House)___ , ___E:Charles Hitchcock Hall U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charles_Hitchcock_Hall)___ , Hotel Del Prado, ___E:Hotel Windermere East U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hotel_Windermere_East)___ , ___E:Frank R. Lillie House U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Frank_R._Lillie_House)___ , ___E:Robert A. Millikan House U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_A._Millikan_House)___ , Poinsettia Apartments, ___E:Promontory Apartments U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Promontory_Apartments)___ , ___E:Jackson Shore Apartments U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jackson_Shore_Apartments)___ , ___E:Frederick C. Robie House U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Frederick_C._Robie_House)___ , ___E:George Herbert Jones Laboratory U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Herbert_Jones_Laboratory)___ , ___E:St. Thomas Church and Convent U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Thomas_Church_and_Convent)___ , ___E:Shoreland Hotel U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shoreland_Hotel)___ , ___E:German submarine U-505 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/German_submarine_U-505)___ , and ___E:University Apartments U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_Apartments_(Chicago,_Illinois))___ .

In addition, the NRHP ___E:Hyde Park-Kenwood Historic District U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hyde_Park-Kenwood_Historic_District)___ and ___E:Jackson Park Historic Landscape District and Midway Plaisance U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jackson_Park_Historic_Landscape_District_and_Midway_Plaisance)___ are located, at least in part, within the Hyde Park community area.

___E:Promontory Point U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Promontory_Point_(Chicago))___ is an artificial ___E:peninsula U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peninsula)___ that extends into ___E:Lake Michigan U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lake_Michigan)___ at 55th Street, providing views of the Downtown Chicago skyline to the north.
Promontory Point is a common location for picnicking, sunbathing, and swimming.

It made news as the location of the wedding reception between ___E:George Lucas U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Lucas)___ and ___E:Mellody Hobson U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mellody_Hobson)___ in June 2013.
The southeastern corner of Hyde Park contains the northern end of ___E:Jackson Park U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jackson_Park_(Chicago))___ .
Jackson Park consists of lagoons surrounding an island in the middle (called the Wooded Island), on which a small ___E:Japanese garden U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Japanese_garden)___ is located.
It is home to a large population of beavers and over two dozen species of birds.

The ___E:Midway Plaisance U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Midway_Plaisance)___ , a wide boulevard that runs from Stony Island Avenue to Cottage Grove Avenue between 59th and 60th streets, connects Jackson Park to ___E:Washington Park U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Washington_Park_(Chicago_park))___ (located to the west of Hyde Park).

Jackson Park has been selected by the ___E:Obama Foundation U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Obama_Foundation)___ as the site of the future ___E:Obama Presidential Center U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama_Presidential_Center)___ .
The shopping areas on 53rd, 55th, and 57th streets host most of the retail businesses in Hyde Park.

53rd Street is Hyde Park's oldest shopping district, lined with many small businesses and restaurants offering various dining options. ___E:Harper Court U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harper_Court)___ , a small-business-oriented shopping center, extends north of 53rd Street along Harper Avenue.
A ___E:farmers' market U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Farmers%27_market)___ is held there in the summer.

The segment of 55th Street between the ___E:Metra U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metra_Electric_District)___ line and the lake offers a series of ethnic restaurants serving Thai, Japanese, and Korean cuisine.
To the west of the Metra line between 54th and 55th streets lies the Hyde Park Shopping Center.

57th Street is noted for its ___E:independent bookstores U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Independent_bookstore)___ . 57th Street also offers restaurants along with small grocery stores, hair stylists, and dry cleaners.
On the first weekend in June, the venerable ___E:57th Street Art Fair U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/57th_Street_Art_Fair)___ takes up 57th Street between Kimbark and Kenwood avenues.

The Hyde Park community area has supported the ___E:Democratic Party U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Democratic_Party_(United_States))___ in the past two presidential elections by overwhelming margins.

In the ___E:2016 presidential election U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_presidential_election_in_Illinois,_2016)___ , Hyde Park cast 10,479 votes for ___E:Hillary Clinton U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hillary_Clinton)___ and 442 votes for ___E:Donald Trump U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Donald_Trump)___ (91.9% to 3.9%).

In the ___E:2012 presidential election U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_presidential_election_in_Illinois,_2012)___ , Hyde Park cast 9,991 votes for ___E:Barack Obama U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama)___ and cast 651 votes for ___E:Mitt Romney U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mitt_Romney)___ (91.4% to 6.0%).

By car, Hyde Park is easily accessed from ___E:Lake Shore Drive U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lake_Shore_Drive)___ , which runs along the neighborhood's easternmost edge. The ___E:Dan Ryan Expressway U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dan_Ryan_Expressway)___ and ___E:Chicago Skyway U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicago_Skyway)___ also lie within a short driving distance.

In terms of public transit, Hyde Park is served by eleven ___E:Chicago Transit Authority U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicago_Transit_Authority)___ bus lines; ___E:Metra U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metra)___ , Chicago's ___E:commuter rail U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Commuter_rail)___ system; and the ___E:South Shore Line U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Shore_Line)___ , an ___E:interurban U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Interurban)___ passenger rail service that runs between Chicago and ___E:South Bend U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Bend,_IN)___ , ___E:Indiana U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indiana)___ .

The latter two use the former ___E:Illinois Central Railroad U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Illinois_Central_Railroad)___ 's embankment in East Hyde Park, near ___E:Lake Michigan U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lake_Michigan)___ .

The ___E:Metra Electric U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metra_Electric)___ —which has three stations in the neighborhood ( ___E:51st/53rd St./Hyde Park U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/51st-53rd_Street_(Hyde_Park)_station)___ , ___E:55th-56th-57th St. U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/55th-56th-57th_Street_station)___ , and ___E:59th St./University of Chicago U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/59th_Street/University_of_Chicago_station)___ )—and the CTA's #6 Jackson Park Express bus provide express service to ___E:the Loop U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicago_Loop)___ from early morning to late night.
The #2 Hyde Park Express and #28 Stony Island busses provide similar service during rush hours.
Off-peak, however, the #2 does not run, while the #28 does so only to points south.

CTA's #10 Museum of Science and Industry route also provides express service to downtown, but only between ___E:Memorial U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Memorial_Day)___ and ___E:Labor Days U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Labor_Day)___ and from one stop at ___E:the museum itself U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Museum_of_Science_and_Industry_(Chicago))___ .

CTA's #15 Jeffrey Local bus runs diagonally through Hyde Park, connecting the neighborhood to points south and to CTA's rapid transit system, the ___E:"L" U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicago_L)___ , at the ___E:Red U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Red_Line_(CTA))___ and ___E:Green Lines U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Green_Line_(CTA))___ ' ___E:47th U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/47th_station_(CTA_Red_Line))___ and ___E:51st St. U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/51st_station)___ stations, respectively.

The #55 Garfield bus runs east–west through the neighborhood, also connecting it to the Red and Green Lines at their respective ___E:Garfield U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Garfield_station_(CTA_Red_Line))___ ___E:stations U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Garfield_station_(CTA_Green_Line))___ , and, ultimately, to Chicago's ___E:Midway Airport U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Midway_Airport)___ .
The #4 Cottage Grove and #X4 Cottage Grove Express bus routes run north–south along Hyde Park's westernmost edge.

CTA also operates three bus routes in collaboration with the University of Chicago: #171 University of Chicago/Hyde Park, #172 University of Chicago/Kenwood, and #192 ___E:University of Chicago Hospitals U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Chicago_Hospitals)___ Express.
The #171 and #172 are local circulator routes that run on a reduced schedule during the summer, while the #192 runs during rush hours only to and from major rail stations in the Loop.

South Shore Line trains stops only at 55th-56th-57th St. They only board passengers southbound and discharge passengers northbound due to a ___E:non-compete agreement U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Non-compete_clause)___ with Metra.
